question: Assume today is 2026-09-14. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in September 2026, as it will be first reported (provisional figure) in the Hong Kong Tourism Board's monthly visitor arrivals press release.

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, worldwide, arrivals counted at immigration/entry, i.e. visitor trips not unique persons) during calendar September 2026, as first reported provisionally by the Hong Kong Tourism Board in its monthly visitor arrivals press release
target.cadence: monthly press release, typically published mid-to-late in the following month (provisional figures)
target.caveats: Period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-14 cutoff, so only partial-month signals (first ~2 weeks) and prior-year/seasonal patterns are usable. Definition is visitor arrivals (trips), not unique visitors; includes same-day in-town visitors and overnight visitors, all nationalities. Excludes

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 arrivals ≈ September 2025 arrivals × (recent YoY growth trend) × (September seasonal factor relative to adjacent months). Own history gives the seasonal shape and the base level; recent months published before cutoff give the momentum.
candidates.data_to_find: HKTB monthly total visitor arrivals for Sep 2023, Sep 2024, Sep 2025 and all months Jan–Jul 2026 (and Aug 2026 if published before 2026-09-14); monthly YoY growth rates; seasonal index of September vs annual average.

assessment.note: p1 is the only kept data point. It gives Jan–May 2026 total visitor arrivals (~23 million), a partial-year level from the HKTB/government source. It is not the target period (September 2026) and cannot be used directly as a September level, but it anchors the 2026 arrival scale and implies a monthly average of roughly 4.6 million for Jan–May 2026. It is a single measurement, so it provides no independent corroboration of itself; any September estimate built from it requires a seasonal and momentum conversion.

p1.role: total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong, Jan–May 2026 (five-month total)

a1.role: September 2026 arrivals as a ratio of the Jan–May 2026 monthly average

methods.rationale: Converts the only kept 2026 level (p1, five-month total) to a monthly average and applies a September seasonal ratio. This is the most direct route given available evidence; its main weakness is that the seasonal ratio a1 is an assumption rather than an observed September-to-average ratio, and it assumes no strong within-2026 trend between Jan–May and September.

p1.role: total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong, Jan–May 2026 (five-month total)

a2.role: September 2026 arrivals as a ratio of the Jan–May 2026 monthly average, incorporating 2026-vs-2025 momentum

methods.rationale: Alternative route using the same p1 base but with a momentum-adjusted ratio a2 that embeds a positive 2026-vs-2025 growth assumption. It shares p1 with m1, so the two are not independent; m2 mainly widens the upper tail to reflect continued recovery. Both methods fail if the Jan–May 2026 average is unrepresentative of September (e.g., a large festival or typhoon effect).

assumptions.name: September share of Jan–May monthly average
assumptions.rationale: September is typically a shoulder month for Hong Kong arrivals: post-summer, pre-October Golden Week, with typhoon risk. Historically September arrivals run somewhat below the summer-peaked monthly average, but Mid-Autumn timing and mainland holiday shifts can push it either way. The Jan–May 2026 average is used as the base because p1 is the only kept 2026 level; the ratio is centered slightly below 1 with a wide range reflecting typhoon and festival-timing uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: The Jan–May 2026 monthly average is a reasonable proxy for the 2026 annual monthly average and September's seasonal deviation is within the stated range.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published September 2025 or 2024 arrivals showing September consistently far above or below the adjacent-month average, or a major policy/typhoon shock in September 2026.

assumptions.name: 2026 vs 2025 momentum factor for September
assumptions.rationale: Hong Kong arrivals have been recovering through 2025–2026; p1's ~23 million in five months implies a strong 2026 run-rate. A modest positive YoY momentum for September 2026 relative to a September 2025 base is plausible, but the exact trend is unobserved, so the range spans flat to strong growth.
assumptions.applies_when: A September 2025 base level is available and 2026 momentum resembles the Jan–May 2026 trend.

The best computed estimate for total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, visitor trips including same-day and overnight) during calendar September 2026, as first provisionally reported by the HKTB, is 4,686,124 visitor (80% model-based interval 2,775,365 to 7,912,387 visitor; too few backtest years, so the interval width comes from Monte Carlo sampling of the formula inputs and reflects input uncertainty only).

The only 2026 anchor is observed point p1, preliminary arrivals for Jan–May 2026 of 23,000,000 visitor arrivals. Both methods convert this to a September figure: m1 (4,375,177 visitor, weight 50%) applies a shoulder-season ratio of 0.95 (range 0.6697 to 1.339) to the five-month monthly average, using 5 months; m2 (5,019,171 visitor, weight 50%) instead applies a momentum factor of 1.08 (range 0.7706 to 1.541). The two share p1 and are not independent; they differ only in framing, hence the equal weighting.

Main risk: p1 is the sole 2026 anchor, so any error propagates directly, and typhoon/festival timing is uncertain. Missing evidence: actual September 2026 daily arrival counts.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 arrivals as ratio of Jan–May 2026 monthly average (seasonal + momentum): 0.95 ratio, range 0.6697 to 1.339 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 arrivals were at or above the spring average (e.g., a major event or festival boost) or a sharp collapse (typhoon, policy shock).
- a2 2026-vs-2025 momentum factor applied to September seasonal ratio: 1.08 ratio, range 0.7706 to 1.541 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Signs of a 2026 slowdown (e.g., flat or negative YoY in mid-2026 monthly releases) or an acceleration well beyond 2025's pace.
- a3 Months in the Jan–May 2026 window: 5 months, range 3.536 to 7.071 (range widened by code); used by m1, m2. Overturned by: Evidence that p1's window is not five months.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
